Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley. Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley is often confused with or conflated with her mother, the philosopher and feminist Mary Wollstonecraft, despite living in different centuries and having distinct legacies. The daughter and author of Frankenstein, Mary Shelley lived from 1797 to 1851 and was a novelist and editor in her own right. Her mother, also Mary Wollstonecraft, lived from 1759 to 1797 and was a polemicist and writer on women's rights who died shortly after Mary's birth.

Mary Wollstonecraft was the philosopher and writer famed for A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, published in 1792, a foundational feminist text advocating women's education and autonomy. Mary Shelley was a novelist best known for Frankenstein, published in 1818, which she conceived during a creative summer in 1816 with her husband Percy Bysshe Shelley.

Mary Shelley was born after her mother's death from complications of childbirth. She never knew Mary Wollstonecraft personally, though her mother's legacy shaped her intellectual upbringing. Mary Shelley married Percy Bysshe Shelley, a Romantic poet, in 1816. After his drowning in 1822, she spent her later life editing his works and writing novels.

The confusion arises because Mary Shelley's full married name honors her mother's name, and both were intellectually accomplished women. Yet their eras and disciplines differ significantly. Mary Shelley also edited a major anthology of her husband's poetry and wrote several other novels beyond Frankenstein, including The Last Man and Mathilda.
